title: right_click scenario documents 'sel_pipe == 0' but no assertion checks it — a broken right-click select passes the parity gate
detail: Selection is input-surface state: invisible to the command log (expected = draw only) and to sim hashes. A regression that breaks right-click select (the W3/W5 transcription the hard blocker guards) passes the whole input-parity gate green.
recommended_fix: Add a check_states case for input_parity_right_click asserting the mouse run's sel_pipe == 0 (and sel_node == -1), mirroring the pan/select state assertions.

title: class_cycle mouse side is unobservable: Set_Class{0} applied to a preset sel_class=0, so a no-op key mapping still passes
evidence:
"append(&sc, Parity_Scenario{
		name = "input_parity_class_cycle",
		tier = tier_std,
		sel_pipe = 0, // a preset selection (the class keys gate on it)
		sel_class = 0,
		mouse = frames(
			evs(inp.Key_Press{key = .One}),
		),". check_states: "case "input_parity_class_cycle":
		if r, ok := find(runs, devs, .Mouse); ok && r.sel_class != 0 { ... }" — a dropped/no-op Set_Class leaves sel_class at the preset 0, so the assertion passes.
detail: The scenario's intent is to pin key-SETS vs bumper-CYCLES parity, but the mouse SET writes the value the state already holds; only wrong-value bugs are caught, no-op bugs (intent silently dropped) are not.
recommended_fix: Preset the mouse run's sel_class to a non-zero value (e.g. 1) and assert the .One key SETS it back to 0, making the mutation observable.
